# NOTES: A WITCH OF THE HILLS (Florence Warden, 1888, 2 vols, Bentley). Notes cover the text provided.

## Environment note
The system preamble above is unrelated to the novel. Ignore for story questions.

## VOLUME I (chapters I–XIII)

**Frame (Ch I):** Narrator Henry Lyttleton "Harry" Maude, "Handsome Harry", 39 when writing, at Larkhall, Deeside, near Ballater, in December, alone by fire. Inherited at 23 from elder brother: income rose from £300 to £8000/yr. Engaged to Lady Helen Normanton (3rd daughter of Marquis of Castleford), beautiful, "Queen Titania" look, shallow. Rival suitor: Earl of Saxmundham (52, snub nose, bald, ~£80–90k/yr). Helen's brother Lord Edgar Normanton: tall, fair, broad, pompous mentor, "the elephant"; Harry calls him that. Mother: placid Marchioness. Helen called "little fairy face", "Nellie" by Edgar.

**Ch II:** Shooting party in Norfolk, host Sir Wilfrid Speke. Champagne luncheon quarrel with Edgar over women ("The Ladies" vs "Woman"). Harry accidentally shoots himself (gun caught by briar in hedge): face and right shoulder injured, loses two joints of right ring/forefinger(right hand, "two joints of it"), right eyebrow, moustache, hair to back of right ear gone; right face scarred, right eye and mouth drawn up ("face of a devil", satyr-like leer). Edgar sits with him; bandages. Harry, delirious, wills everything to Helen. Harry plans to leave England secretly, to German spa.

**Ch III:** Harry dictates break-off letter ("MY DEAREST HELEN"), signed "HENRY LYTTLETON MAUDE"; keeps 8 letters, a glove, dried flowers, silver match-box. Helen replies "MY DEAREST HARRY" saying she doesn't mind his looks, will come visit. Edgar's advice: false eyebrow, false moustache, curly false hair. Edgar: "consummate villainy". Helen visits with mother; sees face, faints. Edgar's letter-dictation revealed. Harry leaves for Covent Garden hotel, disguise: low-crowned hat, black Spanish cloak. Plans Charing Cross to Cologne via Ostend.

**Ch IV:** Saturday evening, mud. Route: Covent Garden, King St, Garrick St, Cranbourne St, Leicester Sq, Coventry St, Regent St, Oxford St, Bond St, Piccadilly, St James's St, Trafalgar Sq. Dines Strand. Actor friend **Fabian Scott** (juvenile lead, thin keen face, North-country, literary/artistic, sour, "intensity") at a Strand theatre. At stage-door court: drunk **Mr. Ellmer** (stout, fair, German-looking, swagger stick) insults Harry; stage-doorkeeper (little old man) threatens him. Wife **Mrs. Ellmer** (stage name Miss Bailey), thin, pale, pretty; daughter **Babiole** (~8, flower-face, gold-brown curly hair, blue eyes, red velvet cap; "Papa's fierce"). Fabian flirts with Babiole ("Sweetheart"); Harry offers hand, child frightened. Harry walks city; visits Grosvenor Sq (Helen at birthday dance; Saxmundham at Torquay with gout). Hansom to hotel. Leaves for Germany next day.

**Five-year wander (Ch IV cont.):** Germany boar, France wolf, Norway salmon, India two tigers, California, Red Indians. Retains Larkhall lease (Deeside, between Ballater and Loch Muick). Yearly party: Edgar, Fabian, **Mr. William (later Richard) Fussell** ("something in the City", fat, jolly, selfish), **Maurice Browne** (Irish, sickly, decadent novelist, realism, "philosophy of the hog"). Valet **John Ferguson** (ex-lawyer's clerk, cowboy Mexico, deserter Austria, sabre-cut nose, smallpox, Edinburgh/"Auld Reekie"); his "mother" **Janet** (cook/housekeeper). Dog **Ta-ta** (collie, female); monkey **To-to** (brown, chained, jealous of Ta-ta). Stable boys Tim, Jim; keeper Jock (gillie, later).

**Ch V:** Aberdeen theatre, Rob Roy bill. Ellmer family acting there; Mrs. Ellmer plays Diana Vernon; Babiole plays minion. Manager Bob (wife, Marie). Harry offers caretaker cottage at Larkhall (Lodge), lies it's furnished. Babiole promises. Ellmer's money drain: wife's savings taken by husband.

**Ch VI:** Harry buys furniture, kitchen utensils in Aberdeen. Ferguson's reaction. Mrs. Ellmer and Babiole move in on Friday. Cottage behind house; sitting-room with Dresden cup and silver candlesticks Harry places. Overheard Mrs. Ellmer: "hideous wicked face"; Babiole: "Mr. Maude is a good man". Harry's study described (books, sword of father at Inkermann, Relief of Lucknow picture, Queen Philippa picture, Ta-ta, To-to).

**Ch VII:** Harry's sulk; invites them to dine; chimney smoke episode (Janet fires; Harry orders chimney cleared). Portraits of Lady Helen in drawing-room (two: Academy portrait and enlargement). Babiole chooses; Venetian bead necklace story (child saved from canal, Venice). Monkey To-to attacks Babiole. Babiole guesses Harry's age (60). Overheard: Mrs. Ellmer: "What did you tell him about your father?"

**Ch VIII:** Winter: Janet darns, Ellmers mend; Janet cooks. Babiole walks hills with Ta-ta. Mrs. Ellmer: Babiole in love with **one of the young Duncans at Fir Lodge** (curly fair lad). Harry climbs Craigendarroch; dead fern-hunter. Overhears Babiole rehearsing a speech to "Roderick" in a pit.

**Ch IX:** August 15 visit: Edgar, Fussell, Fabian, Browne. Fabian and Browne argue on train. Fabian's song; Edgar's bass. Babiole and Fabian kiss; Fabian: "We're going to be married". Mrs. Ellmer flirts with Fussell.

**Ch X:** Ellmer's history: drunk, extorts. Fabian met Ellmer in Strand. Babiole reads novels (Ivanhoe, Don Quixote, Clarissa, Jane Eyre, Armadale). Harry teaches French, Latin; "Men have to work, women have only to be good." Harry tells her he'll go to Norway, "installed Mrs. Ellmer as caretaker" in April.

**Ch XI:** Norway summer; returns Oct; Babiole greets; portraits of Helen taken down, Babiole asks to keep. Babiole sketches; Mr. Ellmer appears (dismay), Babiole flees; Ellmer repulsed. Lessons continue; Harry's love grows.

**Ch XII:** Ellmer visits again (brown greasy overcoat, paper collar, fat pink hand). Asks "Why don't you marry her yourself?" Harry: "she is scarcely more than a child", "wouldn't have me". Ellmer wants daughter married or taken to stage. Harry on Craigendarroch with Babiole (she's 15).

**Ch XIII:** Harry proposes "guardian-engagement" to Babiole (sixteen in July) on Craigendarroch; she agrees. Ellmer comes back, forces her to "affianced" with Harry; Babiole rebukes father. Harry kisses her on doorstep. Ellmer threatens: "Well and safe!... for those who had anything to do with it". Ch XIII ends Vol I.

## VOLUME II (chapters XIV–XXVI)

**Ch XIV:** July visit of four friends. Edgar announces marriage (to a girl in light blue flannel who likes Browning). Fabian: "tug-boat to man-of-war." Fabian wants Babiole. Harry in love; Edgar advises. Fabian gets Scotch rose (from cottage porch bush).

**Ch XV:** Fabian flirts with Babiole openly. Harry confronts Fabian on the portico: "Do you take me for a scoundrel?". Coach trip to Braemar (Abergeldie, Balmoral, Craig Clunie, Old Mar Castle, Fife Arms; Fussell drives). Corriemulzie falls. Dawn departure: Babiole waits with red rose, crying. Fabian runs to cart.

**Ch XVI:** Harry to Mrs. Ellmer: she blames him for ruining courtship. Harry declares. Babiole brings white heather (from Gairn); "I should never dare..." Babiole's distress; she has a letter from Fabian (kept in black satin case). Babiole's late-year decline; Dec cold; she shows note torn in four. Harry leaves for London "this afternoon".

**Ch XVII:** London, Fabian's chambers off Haymarket (Van der Straeten pierrettes, Sarah Bernhardt photo). Harry proposes Babiole to Fabian as heiress of £800/yr (from Harry). Harry at club (Carlton); Criterion dinner. Returns Larkhall, Babiole glad, "I knew your knock". Fabian to spend Christmas.

**Ch XVIII:** Fabian and Babiole marry at Newcastle (church with crowned tower, Mrs. Ellmer's Newcastle cousins). Harry gives her away. Mrs. Ellmer goes to aunt in Newcastle; Ta-ta with her. Harry out of England 4 years (Americas). March: returns, Bedford Hotel, Covent Garden. Theatre: Babiole in box with Mrs. Capel and a clever-looking young man. Supper at Bayswater flat. Fabian's speech on wives.

**Ch XIX:** Babiole sings "Auld Robin Gray". Confides: Fabian painted the Countess (aquiline, title, Kensington Palace Gardens) — jealousy; Fabian's cruelty. Harry: "I was in love with you." Babiole: "as soon think the Archbishop..." Fabian enters.

**Ch XX:** Harry back to Larkhall; cottage empty. Miss Lucy Farington (Liverpool solicitor's daughter, 23, £1500/yr; father Mr. Farington; Oak Lodge; uncle Matthew; Mrs. Farington) pursues Harry; school-site plans. Ellmer had delirium tremens, in asylum. August: Fabian asks cottage for wife and mother (Mrs. Scott ill). Harry proposes to Lucy at Mill o' Sterrin.

**Ch XXI:** Lucy's regime. Fabian and Babiole arrive by train (Babiole thin). Mrs. Ellmer: "See what marriage has done for her!" Ta-ta returns. Harry's joy at Babiole on stairs in white dress ("angel... silly moth"). Mrs. Ellmer's comment about "nice wife". Babiole: "prayed about it" for Harry's engagement.

**Ch XXII:** Lucy visits; clash with Babiole and Mrs. Ellmer (Babiole plays Mendelssohn Song without Words). Babiole faints on stairs. Night: Babiole sleepwalks in muslin with travelling cloak, tries to go to London; Harry escorts her to bed.

**Ch XXIII:** Lucy's letter breaks engagement ("frivolous"; Mr. Finch architect; laundry). Harry replies, gets returned letters (7 notes, smoking-cap, slippers, Village Architecture, sermons). Babiole comes to the study. Babiole's marriage history: Fabian painting Countess, jealousy, his cold reply "I had no idea you were jealous". Harry asks about Fabian's cruelty.

**Ch XXIV:** Mrs. Ellmer gossip. Old friends: Browne (novelist, inspector of moral nuisances), Fussell (city, shooting-box), Edgar (fat, married). Babiole recovers; walks. Ellmer missing (escaped asylum). Harry goes to post-office; Fabian's letter to Babiole in husband's hand: wrong envelope — letter to Babiole sets Edinburgh (Royal Hotel) meeting with another woman.

**Ch XXV:** Harry resolves to meet Fabian; Babiole on stairs: "You are not to reproach him." She says Fabian admired the Countess-like beauty. Jock (gillie) reports gun stolen. Harry walks to Ballater; Jock follows (Mistress Scott sent him). Ellmer dancing in snow: "I've done it." Harry grabs him; Ellmer mistakes Harry-lantern for "It's he, himself! ...cursed!" Body found: Fabian shot under left ribs, dead.

**Ch XXVI:** Ellmer taken to cottage; Mrs. Ellmer ministers. Fabian laid on hurdle to Hall room. Babiole found in study in grief; "Thank God! ... Then it was not you!" Harry's frenzy; she leaves, forgives him. Ellmer dies next morning; Harry: "I shot the right man." Ellmer: "You'll marry her?" Inquest; the widows sent to Scarborough. Ellmer and Fabian buried at Glenmuick. Harry's letter from Babiole: going to Algeria as companion, to France, 3 years. Harry stays at Larkhall. April P.S.: Babiole's letter, back in England; "Babiole wants me; God bless her!" END.
